question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the arc of a circle of radius $3$ centered at the origin traversed counterclockwise from the point $(0,3)$ to the point $(-3,0).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize a part-circle of radius $3$ centered at the origin. This curve can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le \pi .
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+9{sin}^{2}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+9{sin}^{2}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =-9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+27{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =9\operatorname{cos}⁡t(3{sin}^{2}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }9\operatorname{cos}⁡t(3{sin}^{2}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,dt \\  & =9{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t(3{sin}^{2}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,dt \\  & =9{[{sin}^{3}⁡t-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡t}{2}]}_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =9[0-(1-\frac{1}{2})] \\  & =-\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
